properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 2:49PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Minor coastal erosion and high surf conditions are expected for
parts of the West Coast as a Bering Sea low passes by Sunday
through early Tuesday. Primarily South to Southeast wind
directions could help water levels reach 2-4 feet above the mean
high tide level. No flooding is expected.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX out 20 NM; Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 22 at 5:47PM CST until November 22 at 6:15PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
SMWHGX

The National Weather Service in League City has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX out 20
NM...
Waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 615 PM CST.

* At 547 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over Brazos B133, moving northeast at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and large
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves. Large hail could
result in structural damage.

* Locations impacted include...
Brazos B133 and Brazos A70.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 22 at 3:47PM PST until November 23 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations 6 to 12 inches.
Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Olympics.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Inland Kenedy; Coastal Kenedy
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 5:47PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
At 547 PM CST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 7
miles northwest of Kenedy County Wind Farms, or 12 miles southeast of
Sarita, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Kenedy County Wind Farms.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

To report severe weather, contact your nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office in Brownsville.

Service for additional information.

properties.description:
SMWCRP

The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 630 PM CST.

* At 543 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 35 NM southeast of Port Oconnor, moving
northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, large hail, and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves. Large hail could
result in structural damage.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters from Port Aransas to Matagorda Ship Channel from
20 to 60 NM.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with this storm.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 22 at 3:04PM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to
11 feet building to 15 to 22 feet Wednesday with dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible. Most susceptible time of
flooding will be around the time of the morning high tides
between about 800 AM and 1000 AM, especially Wednesday and
Thursday.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 3 PM
PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday
to 3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is the potential for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
coastal structures including piers. Significant beach erosion
is likely. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. The High Surf Advisory
will likely be needed to be upgraded to a High Surf Warning for
Wednesday and Thursday when there will be the potential for
damaging surf. Additional products will likely be needed into

properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 22 at 2:27PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas
along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.3 and 9.8 feet
MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal
Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm
surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the
Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in
King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101
Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 22 at 2:23PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning,
Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW)
at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 22 at 1:33PM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal
astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4
ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides)
combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring
up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and
Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities
of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos
Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway
101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7
PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event
is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January
3rd, 2026.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the high tide periods in the late morning/early
afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as
storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft
and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity
lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which
will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR
tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at
10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM
Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.description:

Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees, power lines, and
unsecured objects. Power outages are possible. Travel could be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways and roads running west to east,
including highway 97, will be exposed to tough driving conditions
given the strong southerly wind speeds. Winds are expected to be
strongest late Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 11:40AM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday,
reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-time tidal
records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the
tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp
increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking
waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing
beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks
to be around 5-8 feet.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through flooded areas.

through early Tuesday. Primarily South to Southeast wind
directions could help water levels reach 2-4 feet above the mean
high tide level. No flooding is expected.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Elevated coastal water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the
normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Coastal Kuskokwim Delta Communities, including Kipnuk,
Kongiganak, and Kwigillingok.

* WHEN...3 AM Sunday to 3 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Elevated coastal water levels driven by southeast
winds gusting to 55 mph. Coastal erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Gusty southeasterly winds will begin
increasing early Sunday morning as the storm approaches.
Highest water levels expected late Sunday night. Winds will
diminish by Sunday evening, and seas will subside by Monday
morning following the natural high tide cycle.
properties.instruction:
Precautions should be taken to protect property, such as securing
or moving property away from the shoreline.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued November 22 at 1:21AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of progressive systems will bring rain to western Washington
starting Tuesday and continuing into the weekend. The heaviest
rainfall is expected late Wednesday into Thursday, with rainfall
amounts over the Olympics ranging generally between 2 to 3 inches.
This will lead to rises on the Skokomish River in Mason County late
Wednesday into Thursday. Flooding will be possible starting midweek
and continuing into the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
